name: Sam Noble Oklahoma Museum of Natural History
unique: A museum with a 40 foot Apatosaurus, a gallery of Oklahoma's Native nations and a working paleontology lab, on the Norman campus.
buzz: The dinosaur hall and the Native galleries are the two routes and the lab is where people linger; it is the best museum in the state for children.

name: Lake Thunderbird
unique: A reservoir east of Norman with a swim beach, boat ramps and trails, the closest big water to Oklahoma City.
buzz: The lake is the summer escape and the fishing is decent; the water is murky and the wind makes afternoon boating choppy.

name: Fried Onion Burger Day
unique: A downtown festival where they cook the world's largest onion fried burger on a giant griddle and the town's burger stands sell them all day.
buzz: The burger history is real and the line for the giant one is the event; El Reno is where the onion burger was invented during the Depression.

name: National Wrestling Hall of Fame
unique: A museum of American wrestling with the honors court, Olympic medals and a gallery on the sport's place in Oklahoma, the state that produces champions.
buzz: Wrestling families plan trips around it and the staff are often coaches; it is small and specific and the sport's history is deeper than outsiders expect.

name: Five Civilized Tribes Museum
unique: A museum in the old Union Agency building on Agency Hill, with art by Cherokee, Choctaw, Chickasaw, Creek and Seminole artists and a collection of historic baskets.
buzz: The art collection is the reason to come and the building is a landmark; the museum is small and the staff are knowledgeable.

name: Honor Heights Park
unique: A hilltop park with 40 acres of azaleas, a duck pond, a miniature train and a view over Muskogee, free and open every day.
buzz: The April azalea festival is the local event and the train is the family draw; the rest of the year it is a quiet picnic park.

name: Cherokee National Museum
unique: The national museum of the Cherokee Nation in the old Cherokee Female Seminary, with the Trail of Tears story, baskets and the Sequoyah syllabary.
buzz: The seminary building and the Trail of Tears gallery are the reasons to come; the nation runs it and the interpretation is from the inside.

name: Oklahoma State Penitentiary Tour
customer: True crime people, history fans, photographers
unique: Tours of a working maximum security prison that has operated since 1908, with the old cell blocks and the death row unit.
buzz: The tours are limited and book out and the guides are corrections staff; it is not a haunted house and the history is heavy.

name: Talimena Scenic Drive
unique: A 54 mile ridge road along the crest of the Ouachita Mountains from Talihina to Mena, Arkansas, with overlooks and switchbacks.
buzz: Motorcyclists rate it among the best rides in the region and the fall color is the season; the road is narrow and fog can close the views.

name: Heavener Runestone
unique: A slab carved with runic letters in a state park, claimed by some as evidence of Vikings and by scholars as a 19th century hoax.
buzz: The ambiguity is the fun and the park is a short walk; the rune stone is behind glass and the setting is a pretty creek valley.

name: Robbers Cave State Park
unique: Sandstone bluffs and caves in the San Bois Mountains where outlaws hid, with CCC built trails, a lake and a horse camp.
buzz: The cave trail and the bluff overlook are the walks and the CCC structures are the architecture; the park is quiet and the trails are rocky.

name: Beavers Bend State Park
unique: A park on the Mountain Fork River below Broken Bow Lake, with trout fishing, a canoe run, pine forest and CCC stonework.
buzz: The trout stream and the kayak run are the reasons to come and the cabins book months ahead; summer weekends are crowded.

name: Broken Bow Lake
unique: A clear reservoir in the Ouachita Mountains with 180 miles of shoreline, pine covered islands and water deep enough for skiing.
buzz: The lake is the summer destination for Oklahoma and Texas and the rentals fill early; the water is clear by Oklahoma standards.

name: Fort Washita
unique: The ruins of a pre Civil War fort on the Washita, with stone buildings, a cemetery and the story of the Chickasaw and Choctaw who settled around it.
buzz: The ruins are evocative and the site is quiet; the reconstruction is limited and the history is the reason to stop.

name: Lake Murray State Park
unique: The oldest and largest state park in Oklahoma, with a lake, CCC stone cabins and trails through the Arbuckle Mountains.
buzz: The CCC cabins and the lake are the draws and the park is busy in summer; the trails are short and rocky.

name: Southern Plains Indian Museum
unique: A museum of Southern Plains beadwork, regalia and paintings by Native artists, in the town that hosts the American Indian Exposition each August.
buzz: The beadwork and the annual exposition are the reasons to visit; it is small and free and the artists are often there.

name: Tallgrass Prairie Preserve
unique: The largest protected remnant of tallgrass prairie left on earth, with a herd of 2,500 bison and a drive through grass that once covered a third of the country.
buzz: The bison herd is the reason to come and the spring wildflowers are the season; the prairie is hot and there is no shade.

name: Eskenazi Museum of Art
unique: A university museum designed by I.M. Pei with a broad collection from ancient to contemporary, free and quiet on the Bloomington campus.
buzz: The building and the ancient galleries are the reasons to stop; it is free and the modern wing rotates often.

name: Lake Monroe
unique: The largest lake in Indiana, with arms running into wooded hills, a beach and a state forest around it.
buzz: The lake is the summer water for Bloomington and the coves are quiet on weekdays; the wind comes up and the water gets rough.

name: Tibetan Mongolian Buddhist Cultural Center
unique: A Tibetan temple in the Indiana hills with a prayer hall, a stupa and a garden, founded by a Tibetan lama who settled in Bloomington.
buzz: Visitors are surprised to find it in Indiana and the gardens are peaceful; the center runs talks and the grounds are free.

name: Fort Wayne Museum of Art
unique: A museum with a strong print and glass collection, in a modern building on Main Street, with a studio space for visitors.
buzz: The print collection and the contemporary glass are the highlights; it is small enough for an hour and the café is a local stop.

name: Foellinger-Freimann Botanical Conservatory
unique: A glass conservatory in downtown with a rainforest, a desert and a seasonally changing garden, warm on a February day.
buzz: The winter escape is the point and the changing displays bring people back; it is small and cheap and connects to the river walk.

name: Fort Wayne Children's Zoo
unique: A zoo designed for children with a train, a carousel, a farm animal area and African lions, built into a wooded park.
buzz: Parents call it one of the best children's zoos in the country and the train is the ritual; it is big enough for three hours.

name: Studebaker National Museum
unique: The collection of the wagon maker that became a car company, with the last Studebaker built, a presidential carriage and the Avanti.
buzz: Car people come for the Avanti and the carriage collection is the surprise; the museum next door covers the same South Bend industrial story.

name: Potawatomi Zoo
unique: The oldest zoo in Indiana, with a train, a carousel and a collection of big cats and hoofed animals in a wooded park.
buzz: The train and the petting zoo are the family draws; it is small and the shade makes a July afternoon bearable.

name: Clabber Girl Museum
unique: The museum and baking store of the baking powder company, with the history of the product, a soda fountain and a test kitchen.
buzz: The soda fountain and the free museum are the stops and the baking aisle is a bargain; it is a quick detour in downtown Terre Haute.

name: Swope Art Museum
unique: A small museum with a surprisingly strong collection of American regionalist painting, including Grant Wood and Thomas Hart Benton, free in downtown Terre Haute.
buzz: Art people call it a hidden collection and it is free; the building is a 1900s library and the galleries are calm.

name: Minnetrista
unique: A 40 acre campus of gardens, a museum and historic buildings on the site of the Ball family estate, with a farmers market and a children's garden.
buzz: The gardens and the farmers market are the local rituals and the museum covers the Ball jar story; the campus is bigger than visitors expect.

name: Columbus Architecture Tour
unique: A small Indiana city with buildings by Eero Saarinen, I.M. Pei, Harry Weese and Robert Venturi, commissioned by a local industrialist after the war.
buzz: Architecture people treat it as a pilgrimage and the self guided tour map is free; the Miller House needs a separate booking.

name: Miller House and Garden
unique: A mid century modern house by Eero Saarinen with interiors by Alexander Girard and a garden by Dan Kiley, kept as the family left it.
buzz: Design people call it one of the best preserved modernist houses in the country; tours are limited and book weeks ahead.

name: Madison Historic District
unique: A Ohio River town of 1,000 preserved buildings from the steamboat era, stacked on the bluffs, with a main street that runs to the water.
buzz: The walk up and down the hill is the visit and the river view is the photograph; the town is quiet on weekdays and busy in summer.

name: Clifty Falls State Park
unique: A gorge of four waterfalls cut into the limestone above the Ohio River, with trails along the creek and a view over the river valley.
buzz: The falls are best after rain and the trails are steep and slick; the park is quiet compared with the state's northern parks.
